meta.dataset: Synthetic ARIS corpus (scripts/generate_dataset.py, seed 2024); eCAR records are OpTC-format, not DARPA OpTC
meta.fpr_definition: FPR = FP / (FP + TN); denominator = all benign parsed events in the test split
label_procedure: ground_truth.json lists one record per injected attack line: host, format, timestamp t, technique.
A parsed event is malicious if it has the same host and format and t <= ts <= t + 120 s.
eCAR/Sysmon: benign records carry random milliseconds, injected ones are whole-second; only whole-second events can match.
auth.log: lines from the six benign generator templates never match.

C2 beacon flows to 192.168.1.10:443 are injected by the generator but absent from ground_truth.json; they are labelled T1071.001, excluded from the primary metrics (neither positive nor negative) and counted as positives in the secondary table.
Matched counts are checked against ground_truth.json per (host, format, t) group.
Incident = (campaign, host, date); detected if any of its events is flagged.

rule_hits.title: System Owner/User Discovery via whoami
rule_hits.description: Detects execution of whoami for local user discovery. Common in early reconnaissance after initial access.

rule_hits.title: Registry Run Key Persistence
rule_hits.description: Detects writes to registry Run keys used for persistence. Attackers add entries here so their payloads execute on user login.

rule_hits.title: Encoded PowerShell Execution
rule_hits.description: Detects PowerShell invocation with encoded commands, a common technique for obfuscation and defense evasion.

rule_hits.title: SSH Brute Force Attempt
rule_hits.description: Detects failed SSH password authentication attempts. Multiple hits from the same source suggest brute force activity.

rule_hits.title: Shadow File Access
rule_hits.description: Detects access to /etc/shadow, the password hash store. Legitimate access is rare outside account management tools.

rule_hits.title: System Information Discovery via systeminfo
rule_hits.description: Detects execution of systeminfo for host reconnaissance. Attackers use this to fingerprint the OS, patch level, and hardware before selecting exploits.

rule_hits.title: RDP Lateral Movement Indicator
rule_hits.description: Detects network connections to TCP port 3389 (RDP) from internal hosts. While RDP is legitimate, connections between workstations (as opposed to from admin jump boxes) may indicate lateral movement.

rule_hits.title: LSASS Memory Credential Dumping
rule_hits.description: Detects credential dumping from LSASS process memory using rundll32 with comsvcs.dll MiniDump, procdump, or direct LSASS access. This is a high-confidence indicator of credential theft.

rule_hits.title: Ingress Tool Transfer via Download or Known Tool Drop
rule_hits.description: Detects PowerShell DownloadString/DownloadFile and IEX patterns used to pull tools from remote hosts, as well as creation of common attacker utilities in temp directories.

rule_hits.title: Obfuscated Execution via mshta or Base64 Decoding
rule_hits.description: Detects execution chains using mshta.exe as a PowerShell parent (a known LOLBin technique) and explicit Base64 decoding in command lines, both indicators of payload obfuscation.

report_audit.union_constraint: Hybrid = Sigma ∪ ML, so FP_hybrid ≥ max(FP_sigma, FP_ml) and TP_hybrid ≤ TP_sigma + TP_ml.
report_audit.explanation: ML-only at P=0.34, R=0.78 implies FP = 1.514·P. The union keeps every ML false positive, so at R=0.89 the hybrid precision is at most 0.89 / (0.89 + 1.514) = 0.370. The reported 0.58 implies FP = 0.644·P, fewer false positives than ML-only alone, which a union cannot have.
report_audit.figure_6_2: IF 'FPR 0.48 at recall 0.40' contradicts IF-only at recall 0.78 with FP = 1.51·P: on one ROC curve FPR cannot fall while recall rises.

external_references.note: LSTM over log-key sequences; needs parsed log templates and sessions.

source_matrix.event_types: Any EventID with Image / CommandLine / ParentImage / TargetObject / DestinationIp / DestinationPort / TargetFilename. Exercised: EID 1 (process create), EID 3 (network connect), EID 13 (registry set).
source_matrix.rules: aris_r_0001 whoami (T1033), 0002 Run key (T1547.001), 0003 encoded PowerShell (T1059.001), 0006 systeminfo (T1082), 0007 RDP 3389 (T1021.001), 0008 LSASS dump (T1003.001), 0009 download cradle (T1105, command-line selections only), 0010 mshta / Base64 (T1027)
source_matrix.limitations: 0009 tool-drop selection matches field file_path, but the parser emits target_filename, so it never fires. Flat JSON only (no Windows XML / EVTX). EventID is not used by any rule, so 0002 also fires on registry reads that carry a Run-key TargetObject.

source_matrix.event_types: Any syslog line matching 'Mon dd HH:MM:SS host daemon[pid]: msg' (sshd, sudo, cron, systemd-logind…); actions classified as auth_failure, auth_success, session_open/close, privilege_escalation.
source_matrix.rules: aris_r_0004 SSH failed password (T1110.001), aris_r_0005 /etc/shadow access (T1003.008)
source_matrix.limitations: Syslog has no year; the parser hard-codes 2024 (wrong for 2025/2026 files and at year rollover). 0004 fires per failed line, with no count or time-window aggregation (engine has no aggregations), so one typo is an alert. Many of the 19 IF features are Windows-only and always 0 here.

source_matrix.event_types: PROCESS CREATE/OPEN, REGISTRY WRITE/READ/DELETE, FLOW OPEN/START, SHELL EXECUTE, FILE CREATE/DELETE/MODIFY, MODULE LOAD, USER_SESSION LOGIN/LOGOUT (other pairs dropped).
source_matrix.limitations: Only validated on generator output, not on the DARPA OpTC release. actorID is not resolved to its process, so FLOW/REGISTRY/FILE events carry no command line or parent. 0009 tool-drop never fires (file_path vs target_filename). No rules for FILE or MODULE events.

score_transform.formula: s(x) = 1 / (1 + exp((f(x) - mu) / sigma)) = sigmoid(-(f(x) - mu) / sigma), rounded to 4 dp
notes: f(x) is IsolationForest.decision_function: lower = more anomalous, so the minus sign is required.
contamination only shifts decision_function by a constant offset, which cancels in (f - mu) / sigma; it has no effect on s(x).
The share of events above 0.5 is set by the skew of f, not fixed at 5% (module docstring was wrong).

throughput.note: Single-core events/second derived from per-component CPU time; excludes DB writes.
